correctness.rationale: One-pole Riemann–Hurwitz and valuation arguments give exactly p(p-1)/2 regular monomials. The Cartier expansion is algebraically exact, including the p-th root of the coefficient. A nonzero coefficient permits row/column scaling to a factorial evaluation matrix, and the polynomial basis/evaluation argument proves each block has rank min(r-ceil(t/2),floor(t/2)+1), whose complete sum is (p²-1)/8. When a=0 all possible terms contain positive powers of a^(1/p). The standalone checker independently verified primes 3,5,7,11,13,17,19 (3 is a known non-novel control). No finite experiments were used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The a-number is a natural fine Jacobian invariant not fixed by genus and geometric p-rank. This is a full parameter-uniform infinite-prime classification on the non-Hermitian locus of a family singled out by an exceptional large Heisenberg automorphism group, with a sharp jump at the Hermitian point. The exact invariant serves moduli-stratum and p-torsion investigations and is not a routine reformulation of known automorphism or genus results.
